prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an outdoor nighttime courtyard layout with a table and plastic bag in the bottom-left foreground (brightest white, ~0.3–0.6 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach), a metal chair at bottom-right (~0.8–1.2 m), a standing man in the centre holding a food cone/cup (~1.2–1.8 m away in frame 1), a bicycle helmet mounted behind the table at left (~1.2–1.5 m), and a bench, palm tree, and building wall receding behind the man (~2.5–6 m, dark grey) against a black background (>10 m). Across the five frames, the man's silhouette brightens and shifts downward and slightly right as he steps closer (from ~1.8 m to ~1.0 m), turns his torso slightly left in frame 3, and lowers himself into the metal chair beside the table in frames 4–5 (~0.5 m from the bag and table edge), while keeping the cone in his right hand and reaching his left arm down to the chair armrest. Because of the low-light RGB exposure, the depth map makes it much easier to separate the dark-clothed man, the black helmet on the left, the palm trunk, and the background bench from the dark building and sky behind them. However, the map is unreliable around thin or porous structures such as the slatted metal chair back, which merges into a solid blob, and it merges the held food item seamlessly into the man's hand and torso silhouette while losing all detail in the distant illuminated walkway.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates a single 'person' mask in the centre of all five frames (~1.8 m from the camera wearer in frame 1, approaching to ~1.0 m and sitting down by frame 5) along with intermittent background and foreground objects: the metal chair at bottom-right (~1.0–1.2 m away, just to the man's left and below his left hand) in frame 1, the dark bench behind him to the right (~3–4 m away, ~1.5–2.5 m behind the man) in frames 2 and 3, and the hanging helmet on the left (~1.3 m away, ~0.8 m to the man's right) in frame 5. As the man approaches and sits across frames 1 to 5, his mask shifts downward, widens in frame 4 as his left elbow extends outward over the chair, and increasingly occludes the metal chair beneath him and the lower palm trunk behind him, while his legs remain cropped out below the bottom edge of the frame. The map provides crisp 2D object boundaries for the man and the dark background bench in frames 2–3 that are nearly invisible against the dark pavement in the RGB image. However, it is highly unreliable in class labelling and recall: it misclassifies the foreground metal chair as a 'tennis racket' in frame 1 and the helmet as a 'parking meter' in frame 5, merges the held food cone into the 'person' mask, and completely misses the foreground table and plastic bag within the wearer's reach.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the single man in front of the camera wearer (~1.8 m away in frame 1 to ~1.0 m in frame 5), showing his head, torso, and both arms while his lower body below the hips is out of view or unestimated. Across frames 1 to 3, the yellow torso polygon and facial keypoints show him facing mostly toward the camera wearer before turning slightly toward the left of the frame in frame 3 as he approaches, with his right elbow bent upward holding the food item (~0.3 m in front of his chest) and his left arm extended down toward the chair (~0.4 m to his left, within his arm's reach). In frame 4, the skeleton bends sharply downward as he lowers himself onto the chair, with a dense magenta hand cluster appearing on his raised right hand near the table (~0.8 m from the camera wearer) and his left arm angled out and down onto the chair backrest; by frame 5 he is seated upright facing forward and looking down toward the food in his right hand. The skeleton makes the man's torso twist, shoulder tilt, and left-arm support posture clearly readable despite his dark shirt blending into the night background in RGB. However, the map is unreliable in frame 2 where the right hip keypoint collapses inward to form a twisted torso triangle, in frame 4 where the torso collapses into a single horizontal line without hips, and across frames 1–3 and 5 where the magenta hand mesh fails to detect on his right hand.
